identity.title: The ALMA Spectroscopic Survey in the HUDF: the Molecular Gas Content of Galaxies and Tensions with IllustrisTNG and the Santa Cruz SAM

paper_type_evidence.quote: We compare results from ASPECS to predictions from two cosmological galaxy formation models: the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical simulations and the Santa Cruz semi-analytic model (SC SAM).

targets.name: Hubble Ultra Deep Field (ASPECS 3 mm survey area)

evidence.quote: The 3 mm campaign discussed here scanned a contiguous area of $\sim4.6$ arcmin$^2$ in the frequency range 84–115 GHz

question.value: Do IllustrisTNG and the Santa Cruz SAM reproduce the H2 content of galaxies measured by ASPECS (H2 mass vs stellar mass, H2 mass function, H2 cosmic density), after accounting for sensitivity limits and field-to-field variance?

evidence.quote: We will specifically try to quantify the success of these different galaxy formation evolution models in reproducing the observations by accounting for sensitivity limits, field-to-field variance effects, and systematic theoretical uncertainties.
is an ALMA Large Program (Program ID: 2016.1.00324.L) which consists of two scans, at 3 mm and 1.2 mm.

bands.value: 3 mm scan, 84–115 GHz (the 1.2 mm scan is not used here)

evidence.quote: The 3 mm campaign discussed here scanned a contiguous area of $\sim4.6$ arcmin$^2$ in the frequency range 84–115 GHz
encompassed a volume of 338 Mpc$^3$, 8198 Mpc$^3$, 14931 Mpc$^3$, 18242 Mpc$^3$, in CO(1-0), CO(2-1), CO(3-2), CO(4-3), respectively.

angular_resolution.value: line-search cube beam ≈1.75'' x 1.49''; spectra extracted from cube smoothed to ~3.5''

evidence.quote: The line-search is performed in a cube with a synthesized beam of $\approx 1.75'' \times 1.49''$.

evidence.quote: of $\sim 2\times10^9$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$ (assuming a line width of 200 km s$^{-2}$) at virtually any redshift $z>1$

evidence.quote: in particular the redshift catalog provided by the MUSE HUDF survey ((cite: Bacon2017), (cite: Inami2017))

evidence.loc: 4.2 The evolution of the H2 mass function
evidence.quote: we compare the model predictions to the results from ASPECS, as well as the results from the COLDZ survey at $z\sim2.6$

what.value: ASPECS line detections, luminosities, volumes, mass functions and cosmic density

evidence.quote: Details of this analysis are presented in (cite: Decarli2019) and (cite: Boogaard2019).

what.value: z=0 observed H2 masses of galaxies

evidence.quote: the predictions are compared to observed H$_2$ masses of galaxies from (cite: Saintonge2017) at $z=0$

what.value: PHIBBS compilation of H2 masses at higher z

evidence.quote: a compilation presented in (cite: Tacconi2018) as a part of the PHIBBS (IRAM Plateau de Bure HIgh-z Blue Sequence Survey) survey

evidence.quote: The mass functions at $z=0$ are compared to observations taken from from (cite: Keres2003), (cite: Obreschkow2009), (cite: Boselli2014), and (cite: Saintonge2017).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: IllustrisTNG TNG100 (~100 Mpc)^3 simulation and Santa Cruz SAM on Bolshoi merger trees, with H2 recipes GK, K13, BR

evidence.quote: In this paper we use and analyze the TNG100 simulation, a $\sim$(100 Mpc$)^3$ cosmological volume simulated with the code AREPO

what.value: SC SAM model parameters same as SPT15 except alpha_rh=2.6 and kappa_AGN=3.0e-3

evidence.quote: The model parameters adopted in this work are the same as in SPT15, except for $\alpha_{\rm rh} = 2.6$

what.value: ASPECS line identification, luminosities and CO SLED treatment

evidence.quote: The line luminosities are then transformed into corresponding CO(1-0) luminosities based on the (cite: Daddi2015) CO SLED template

what.value: SC SAM metallicity and H2 floors

evidence.loc: 2.5 Metallicity and molecular hydrogen fraction floor in the SC SAM
evidence.quote: Following PST14 and SPT15, we adopt a metallicity floor of $Z=10^{-3}\,$Z$_\odot$ and a floor for the fraction of molecular hydrogen of $f_{\rm mol}=10^{-4}$.

unstated_but_needed: Exact ASPECS catalog values (line luminosities, redshifts, mass-function points) are taken from companion papers; they are not tabulated here
Code and settings used to post-process TNG100 (cell selection, subhalo handling) are not given
How mass functions were binned and how the 1000 random cones were placed, beyond the stated number
Cosmology parameters are only said to be consistent with Planck 2016
Stellar-mass cuts and the SFR main-sequence selection at z=0 are only partly specified

analysis_steps.goal: Compute H2 fractions for model galaxies

method.value: Apply the GK (main), K13 and BR H2 partitioning recipes to TNG100 gas cells and to SC SAM annuli

evidence.quote: In this paper we present predictions for the H$_2$ properties of galaxies by adopting three different molecular hydrogen fraction recipes.

key_parameters.value: TNG100 f_H=0.76; T_SF=1000 K; Sigma_SFR,MW=0.004 Msun/yr/kpc^2

evidence.quote: we simply assume a hydrogen fraction for the gas cells of $f_{\rm H} = 0.76$.
is assumed to be equal to the gas-phase metallicity expressed in solar units, i.e., $D_{\rm MW} = Z/Z_\odot$

validation.value: Compared the three recipes with each other; differences minimal

evidence.quote: Given the minimal deviations in the medians between the different H$_2$ partitioning recipes, we will show from now on only predictions by the GK partitioning method

analysis_steps.goal: Define galaxy H2 mass and apply the ASPECS selection

method.value: Use 'Grav' and 3.5 arcsec apertures ('In2Rad' at z=0); apply an ASPECS CO sensitivity cut for 200 km/s lines

evidence.loc: 2.4 The H2 mass of a galaxy in IllustrisTNG
evidence.quote: The second only accounts for the H$_2$ mass of cells that are within a circular aperture with a diameter corresponding to 3.5 arcsec on the sky

key_parameters.value: ASPECS sensitive to H2 ~1e9 Msun at z=0.29 and ~1e10, 2e10, 3e10 Msun at z≈1.43, 2.61, 3.8

evidence.quote: ASPECS is sensitive to sources with an H$_2$ mass of $\sim 10^9\rm\rm{M}_\odot$ at $z=0.29$ and $\sim 10^{10},\,2\times 10^{10},\,$and $3\times10^{10}\,\rm{M}_\odot$

assumptions.value: alpha_CO = 3.6 Msun/(K km/s pc^2); line width 200 km/s

evidence.quote:
we adopt the same CO excitation conditions and CO–to–H$_2$ conversion factor as ASPECS, $\alpha_{\rm CO} =
    3.6\,\rm{M}_\odot/(\rm{K}\,\rm{km/s}\,\rm{pc}^{2})$, and assume a CO line-width of 200 km/s.

method.value: Compute mass function and cosmic density in 1000 random cones matching the ASPECS volume at each redshift

evidence.loc: 4.2.1 Field-to-field variance effects on the H2 mass function
evidence.quote: in 1000 randomly selected cones through the simulated volume that capture a volume corresponding to the actual volume probed by ASPECS at the given redshifts

evidence.loc: 5.1.2 The CO–to–H2 conversion factor and CO excitation conditions
evidence.quote: We show the H$_2$ mass of galaxies as a function of stellar mass when varying the CO–to–H$_2$ conversion factor
IllustrisTNG is a cosmological, large-scale gravity+magnetohydrodynamical simulation based on the moving mesh code AREPO

used_for.value: halo finding in the Bolshoi merger trees for the SC SAM

evidence.quote: Dark matter haloes were identified using the ROCKSTAR algorithm

results_numeric.quantity: H2 mass of z>1 galaxies predicted vs observed (alpha_CO=3.6)

evidence.quote: the H$_2$ mass of $z>1$ galaxies predicted by the models as a function of their stellar mass is a factor of 2–3 lower than observed

results_numeric.quantity: Reduction in H2 cosmic density from applying ASPECS limit at z=1

evidence.quote: the H$_2$ cosmic density is a factor of three (an order of magnitude) lower at $z=1$ ($z>2$)

can be alleviated by adopting a CO–to–H$_2$ conversion factor in the range $\alpha_{\rm CO} =
2.0 - 0.8\,\rm{M}_\odot/(\rm{K}\,\rm{km/s}\,\rm{pc}^{2})$

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of TNG realizations reproducing ASPECS rho(H2) at z~1.43

evidence.loc: 4.3.1 Field-to-field variance effects on the H2 cosmic density
evidence.quote: only up to 2.5% of the realizations drawn from IllustrisTNG reproduce the ASPECS observations

findings_qualitative.value: Systematic uncertainty between the H2 partitioning recipes is minimal

evidence.quote: The systematic uncertainty between different H$_2$ partitioning recipes for predictions of the H$_2$ mass of galaxies, the H$_2$ mass function, and the H$_2$ cosmic density of the Universe is minimal.

claims.hypothesis: Do the models produce enough H2 per stellar mass at z>1?
claims.experiment: Compare model H2–M* relations with ASPECS and PHIBBS using the ASPECS selection
claims.result: Models are 2–3 times lower; many detections lie outside the 2-sigma scatter
claims.finding: Models underpredict H2 at z>1 for alpha_CO=3.6

evidence.quote: the typical H$_2$ masses of galaxies at $z>1$ as a function of their stellar mass predicted from IllustrisTNG and the SC SAM are lower than the observations by a factor of 2–3.

claims.hypothesis: Do the models reproduce the cosmic H2 density once selection and variance are included?
claims.experiment: Cosmic density in 1000 ASPECS-volume cones with sensitivity limits
claims.result: TNG in tension; SC SAM only just agrees
claims.finding: Predicted cosmic densities appear too low

evidence.quote: The predictions by the SC SAM and IllustrisTNG for the H$_2$ cosmic density only just agree with the ASPECS results after taking field-to-field variance effects into account.

claims.hypothesis: Can a different alpha_CO resolve the tension?
claims.result: Better agreement, but 0.8 is unrealistic and overpredicts z=0 H2
claims.finding: alpha_CO~2 plausibly alleviates much of the tension

evidence.quote: would alleviate much of the tension between model predictions by IllustrisTNG and the SC SAM and the ASPECS results

why_this_method.value: Model predictions allow estimating selection functions and field-to-field variance for ASPECS

evidence.quote: Theoretical models can be used to estimate limitations in the observations (e.g., field-to-field variance, selection functions)

limitations_admitted.value: ASPECS covers only 4.6 arcmin^2, so field-to-field variance is large

evidence.loc: 5.2 Field-to-field variance and selection effects for ASPECS
evidence.quote: it is by far not large enough to overcome significant uncertainties due to field-to-field variance

referee_caveats_inferred: Fixed 200 km/s line width simplifies the selection function
Fixed f_H=0.76 and Jeans-length surface densities in TNG are crude
Observed ASPECS H2 values depend on assumed CO SLED and alpha_CO, so the tension is partly observational
